  AI orchestration is supposed to be the future, and right now
  everyone says Sakana Fugu is the new king. 15 million views. Top of
  every benchmark. I spent real hours inside it. This is the honest
  review nobody else is giving you.

  Here's the idea. Most AI runs one model, then quietly downgrades you
  to a cheaper one to save money. Fugu flips that. It loads only
  flagship models: Opus 4.8, Codex, Gemini. It breaks your prompt into
  separate tasks and routes each one to whichever model does it best.
  In theory you get the best of all three, with results past even
  Fable 5.

  In practice, Opus 4.8 is just the best model out there. So most jobs
  route straight to Opus anyway. You end up with a 4.8 result that's
  maybe one or two percent sharper on the rare task where Codex or
  Gemini edges ahead. That's the whole gain.

  Now the cost. A reply that takes Claude ten seconds can take Fugu
  eight minutes. It runs five times more expensive. Ten times slower
  for two percent better, and that maths doesn't work. In that wait
  you could iterate with one model and close the gap yourself.

  Orchestration still wins eventually. Routing every task to the right
  model is where AI is going, in business, in crypto, in every
  decision we make. Sakana Fugu just isn't the version worth your time
  yet.

The hedge fund method is how quants actually trade — and it has nothing to do with trend lines, indicators, or vibes. It's a Markov regime model that quantifies the market into three states: bull, bear, and sideways. And once you see it, you can't unsee it.

Here's the core. You label every day in an asset's history based on the trailing 20-day return — 5% or more is a bull state, -5% or worse is a bear state, everything else is sideways. Then you count every transition between states and turn those counts into a 3x3 transition matrix of probabilities. That matrix tells you the odds of tomorrow's regime based only on today.

This is the opposite of how retail trades. You're not guessing. You're calculating. The Markov property says the past doesn't matter — only the current state determines what comes next, and the stickiness of each regime tells you how to size the trade.

I'll walk you through squaring the matrix for multi-day forecasts, the stationary distribution that explains why 28-day predictions collapse, signal generation by subtracting bear probability from bull probability, and the walk-forward backtest that stops your strategy from cheating with future data. Then the hidden Markov model removes the subjective labels entirely.

You'll get a free Claude Code skill and a Pine Script overlay for TradingView — copy, paste, done. This is real quant Mark
